title: Struct Basics
concept: A package that combines multiple variables into one (user-defined type)

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
Header for using `printf`.

This lesson covers structure definition, member access, and copy operations.

steps.title: Definition of structure ‘frame’
steps.explanation:
`struct Point { int x; int y; };` is a new type blueprint with two members.

This step is a type definition and no actual variable memory is created yet.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

Afterwards, create a structure variable to check the value and copy operation.

steps.title: Declare and initialize structure variables
steps.explanation:
The actual variable `p1` is created and its members are initialized with `struct Point p1 = {10, 20};`.

You can manage a bunch of related data with one variable name.

steps.title: Access and output structure members
steps.explanation: Access `p1.x` and `p1.y` using the dot operator (`.`) to read the values.

steps.title: Copy structure (copy value)
steps.explanation:
A copy of the form `p2 = p1` copies the member value to a new variable.

The original and the copy will henceforth exist independently.

steps.title: Modify copied structure members
steps.explanation: If you change a member of copy `p2`, the change only applies to the copy.

steps.title: Check the original (p1) value
steps.explanation:
If you check the original values ​​again, they will remain in their previous state.

This is key evidence showing that it was a value copy.

steps.title: Check copy(p2) value
steps.explanation: The copy retains the modified values ​​and is separate from the original.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Key point: Struct assignment is copying values, and member access uses the `.` operator.

quiz.question: What operator accesses structure members?
quiz.explanation:
When entering a member from the variable itself, use a dot (`.`).
For pointers, use an arrow (`->`).

misconceptions.wrong: The size of a structure is the sum of the sizes of its members.
misconceptions.correct: This is mostly correct, but may be larger due to padding.
misconceptions.why: In order for the CPU to read data quickly, it aligns the lines by inserting empty space (padding) in between (Memory Alignment).

keyTakeaway: Let's group related data into `struct`. If you use `=`, the entire value is copied.
